title: Improving Access to and Sustainability of the Rare Disease Fund
what_it_is: Improving Access to and Sustainability of the Rare Disease Fund

sections.label: Rare Disease Fund established
sections.summary: MOH and SingHealth Fund jointly established the RDF in July 2019 to provide supplemental financial assistance for rare disease treatment at public institutions.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Jointly established by the Ministry of Health (MOH) and SingHealth Fund in July 2019, RDF aims to ensure affordability in treatment costs for Singapore Citizens with rare diseases through providing supplemental financial assistance for those who still require it after Government subsidies, insurance and financial assistance, with the premise that treatment is sought at public healthcare institutions.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: According to the Agency for Care Effectiveness (ACE), there are over 2,000 Singaporeans with rare diseases and 700 of them being children.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Treatment and medications for rare diseases are for life, with expenses ranging from tens of thousands per month to over half a million per year.

sections.label: RDF beneficiary numbers
sections.summary: Six beneficiaries were supported with $2 million, and by April 2021 the number had increased to seven.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Six beneficiaries are supported with a total of $2 million and, by April 2021, the number of beneficiaries has increased to seven.

sections.label: Neuroblastoma and Krabbe Disease
sections.summary: Neuroblastoma accounts for about 5.3% of childhood cancers in Singapore, and 43 Singaporeans are known to have Krabbe Disease.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Neuroblastoma accounts for about 5.3% of all childhood cancers diagnosed in Singapore annually, equivalent to about 15 children from March 2017 to February 2019, and with the cost of treatment going upwards of $1 million and some of the specialist treatments not available in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, Krabbe Disease is a hereditary genetic disorder and 43 Singaporeans are known to have this.

sections.label: RDF funding sources
sections.summary: Besides the seed fund, the RDF relies heavily on community donations matched by a Government grant, with eventual reliance on investment returns.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Apart from the seed fund, the RDF is heavily reliant on community donations matched by the Government grant, with eventual reliance on investment returns.

sections.label: Insurance and pre-existing conditions
sections.summary: Many rare disease patients rely on insurance, but many products exclude pre-existing conditions or charge very high premiums for them.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Many of those with rare diseases do heavily rely on insurance to manage medical costs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: However, the knotty situation is that many insurance products excludes pre-existing conditions, and even if the insurance does allow for some pre-existing conditions, it comes at a very high premium.

sections.label: Insurance coverage and premium options
sections.summary: The passage asks whether insurers could cover rare disease patients under higher co-payment, or the RDF partially offset insurance premiums.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: In order to allow for better access to medical insurance and a more manageable and sustainable insurance premiums for those with rare diseases, can insurance companies consider providing coverage under a higher co-payment condition for those with rare diseases?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Alternatively, could the RDF be explored to partially offset the cost for the insurance premium in order to assist them?

sections.label: RDF necessity and inclusiveness
sections.summary: The RDF is necessary and helpful for rare disease patients, but it is timely to ask if it met its objectives and how to be more inclusive.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: To conclude, Mr Deputy Speaker, the RDF is indeed necessary and very helpful for those with rare diseases.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: However, it is timely that we ask whether RDF has achieved its initial objectives and what more can we do to make it more inclusive.

sections.label: Government matching to establish RDF
sections.summary: In 2019 the Government matched $3 for every $1 of public donation to establish the RDF as a charity fund for Singapore Citizens with rare genetic diseases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The Government shares her concern for individuals with rare diseases where medication is very costly and required for life.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: This was why, in 2019, the Government provided a generous matching of $3 for every $1 of public donation to establish the RDF as a charity fund to support Singapore Citizens diagnosed with rare genetic diseases.

sections.label: Six medicines covered
sections.summary: In two years, six medicines have been covered.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In two years, we have covered six medicines.

sections.label: RDF grant payouts
sections.summary: Last financial year the RDF paid grants of around $1 million, and this financial year projects around $1.5 million, 50% more for the same patients.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In the last financial year alone, the RDF made grant payouts of around $1 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: For example, in this financial year, RDF is projecting to make grant payouts of around $1.5 million, which is 50% more than the last financial year for the same group of patients.

sections.label: Fundraising support and tax deductions
sections.summary: The Government matched donations $3-to-$1, gave 250% tax deduction, and funds all RDF administrative costs so every donation cent goes to patients.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: It is not easy raising funds for patients with rare diseases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: It was in recognition of this difficulty that the Government decided to match donations $3-to-$1, so that every donation dollar is stretched further and also to help encourage donors to come forward.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In addition, all donations to the RDF are also eligible for a generous level of tax deduction at 250% and the Government also funds all administrative costs of the RDF so that donors are assured that every single cent of their donation goes to the patients.

sections.label: Pipeline of five medicines
sections.summary: The RDF Committee has a pipeline of five other medicines for three more rare diseases, ready once sufficient funds are raised.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Currently, the RDF Committee has a pipeline of five other medicines for three more rare diseases that stand ready to be added to the RDF list once sufficient funds are raised.

sections.label: MediShield Life rare disease coverage
sections.summary: MediShield Life covers all Singaporeans from birth with no disease exclusions, including rare diseases, subject to claims limits.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In addition, our universal national medical insurance, MediShield Life, covers all Singaporeans from birth, with no disease exclusions, including all rare diseases, subject to the relevant claims limit.
